editorial.headline: The Quiet Machinery of Government Administration
editorial.standfirst: A tightly defined government-administration activity, closed to foreign investment nationally and unavailable for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity is the administrative machinery behind government functions that sit outside the more specifically defined parts of public administration. It covers other government institutions, agencies and bodies with particular duties, together with their secretariats, where their role is to help government operate smoothly. That can include non-structural institutions: bodies created for a defined public purpose whose work still requires an administrative home, coordination and secretariat support.

The scope is therefore institutional rather than commercial. It is concerned with public bodies carrying out special assignments and with the administrative arrangements that allow those assignments to function. The record does not identify any business scale open to registration for this activity. That absence matters: this is not presented as a general-purpose private-sector category, but as a defined part of the government-administration landscape.

Nationally, the position is unequivocal. The activity is closed to PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 0%. Foreign capital has no registration route under this activity at the national level. Bali does not alter that conclusion: the Bali status is also closed, and a foreigner cannot register this activity in Bali today. The Bali record adds an important distinction, however. Its closed position is not attributed to the province-wide moratorium for low and medium-low risk activities; this activity is recorded as medium-high or high risk and its treatment must be verified for the specific address. That is an address-level verification point, not an opening for PMA registration.

For founders and advisers, the useful reading is disciplined rather than speculative. The activity belongs to the public-administration sphere described in its scope, has no listed open scale, and is closed to foreign investment. In Bali, the same closed status applies, while the reason makes clear that the island-wide moratorium is not the operative explanation. The practical conclusion remains the same: this is not a PMA registration path.
